considered a part of the subject. In the given sentence, ‘The
teacher’ is the subject, which is singular. Therefore, ‘were’ must
be replaced with ‘was’. Hence, ‘along with the students was
crossing’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She is allergic from peanuts, so she always checks food labels carefully.
questions.explanation:
(b) She is allergic to peanuts
‘To’ is a fixed preposition used with the adjective ‘allergic’.
Hence, ‘allergic to peanuts’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The doctor prescribes antibiotics and a cough syrup to me when I had severe cough and cold.
questions.explanation:
(d) prescribed
The given sentence is in the past tense, therefore the past
form(V ) of the verb will be used. Hence, ‘prescribed(V )’ is the
2 2
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She runs more faster than her brother in the track events.
questions.explanation:
(a) runs faster than
We generally use the comparative degree with ‘than’ to make a
comparison between two persons or things. ‘Faster’ is the
correct comparative degree of ‘fast’. Therefore, ‘more’ will be
removed. Hence, ‘runs faster than’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Traffic is always remaining heavy in this part of Delhi.
questions.explanation:
(d) always remains
Simple present tense is used to denote conditions that are
generally true. The given sentence talks about the general
condition of traffic in a part of Delhi. ‘Traffic’ is a singular subject
that will take ‘remains’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘always
remains’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I saw that movie last week and it was really interesting.
questions.explanation:
(b) No improvement required
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The movie was not only interesting but also it was very suspenseful.
options: but also it is very suspenseful
questions.explanation:
(d) but also very suspenseful
‘Not only … but also’ is a pair conjunction and the same part of
speech is used after them. There is an adjective after ‘not only’,
so we will use an adjective after ‘but also’. ‘Suspenseful’ is an
adjective. Hence, ‘but also very suspenseful’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Since last evening, the boy has been complaining with pain in his legs.
questions.explanation:
(a) of
‘Of’ is used after the verb ‘complain’ to indicate the issue or the
problem. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘of’ has been used to
indicate the pain. Hence, ‘of’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He asked the speaker some questions until the session.
questions.explanation:
(a) during
‘During’ is used to indicate the time at which something
happens, which is usually an event or an activity. Similarly,
‘session’ is the event in which he asked the speaker some
questions. Hence, ‘during’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Last evening I have gone to the theatre to see a performance.
questions.explanation:
(b) I went
The given sentence is in the simple past tense, therefore the
past form(V ) of the verb will be used. Hence, ‘went(V )’ is the
2 2
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: John was absent from the meeting because he was sick, nor did he inform anyone.
options: and did not he inform anyone
but he did not inform anyone
questions.explanation:
(d) but he did not inform anyone
‘But’ is used to indicate a contrast between expectation and
reality. A sick person is expected to inform somebody regarding
the leave but in the given sentence John did not inform anyone.
Hence, ‘but he did not inform anyone’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Linguists say that this method helps accelerate language learning.
questions.explanation:
(a) No improvement required
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Identify the errors in the given sentence and choose the sentence that rectifies these errors. I have known her for many years. This time, she took unusual decision in unprejudiced way.
options: I have known her for many years. This time, she took an unusual decision in a unprejudiced way.
I have known her for many years. This time, she took an unusual decision in an unprejudiced way.
I have known her for many years. This time, she took a unusual al decision decision in in an unprejudiced way.
I have known her for many years. This time, she took unusual decision in an unprejudiced way.
questions.explanation:
(b) I have known her for many years. This time, she took
an unusual decision in an unprejudiced way.
Article ‘an’ is used before words starting with a vowel sound (an
apple, an umbrella, an American). Similarly, in the given
sentence, the words ‘unusual’ and ‘unprejudiced’ start with a
vowel sound. Hence, the sentence given in option (b) is correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: My mom made her muffins, but she didn't eat none.
questions.explanation:
(c) she didn’t eat any
‘None’ is not used in a negative sentence. ‘None’ must be
replaced with ‘any’ as we use ‘any’ in a negative sentence.
Hence, “she didn’t eat any” is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Identify the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the given options. Tide pool is a isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as tide goes out.
options: A tide pool is a isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as a tide goes out.
A tide pool is an isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as the tide goes out.
Tide pool is isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as a tide goes out.
The tide pool is isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as tide goes out.
questions.explanation:
(b) A tide pool is an isolated pocket of water that is
formed when sea water becomes trapped as the tide goes out.
Indefinite article ‘a/an’ is used when we talk about a noun in
general. Similarly, the given sentence talks about ‘tide pool’ and
‘isolated pocket’ in a general sense. We will use article ‘a’ before
‘tide’ (consonant sound) and article ‘an’ before ‘isolated’(vowel
sound). Article ‘the’ will be used before the 2nd ‘tide’. Hence, the
sentence given in option (b) is correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He behaves if he were a king.
questions.explanation:
(c) behaves as if
‘As if’ is used to talk about a situation that may not be true but
that is possible. Similarly, in the given sentence, the person may
not be a king but he behaves like a king. Hence, ‘behaves as if’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: What do you like to do on your free days other than to watching movies?
questions.explanation:
(b) watching movies
We use a noun, pronoun or a gerund(V ) after the phrase ‘other
ing
than’. Therefore, ‘to’ will be removed. Hence, ‘watching(V )
ing
movies’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the correct version of the following sentence. He would be meet us next week.
options: He would be meets us next week.
He would not be met us next week.
He will be meet us next week.
He will be meeting us next week.
questions.explanation:
(d) He will be meeting us next week.
The given sentence is in the future continuous tense and follows
the structure, “Third person pronoun + will + be + V ing ”. Hence,
the sentence given in option (d) is correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: While I was waiting for Asha for shopping, I spilled lemonade on my new trousers
questions.explanation:
(b) to shop
Infinitive(to + V ) is used after the verb ‘wait’. Therefore, ‘for
1
shopping’ must be replaced with ‘to shop(V )’. Hence, ‘to shop’ is
1
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Whether she wishes to relocate to Mumbai or continues to live here are her personal decisions.
questions.explanation:
(a) is her personal decision
‘Whether … or’ is a pair of conjunctions. According to the “Rule of
Proximity”, the verb is supplied according to the subject closest
to the verb. In the given sentence, the close subject is a verb
phrase ‘continues to live’, which denotes a single action.
Therefore, singular verb ‘is’ will be used. Hence, ‘is her personal
decision’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He gave his heart and soul to make the entire show a success.
questions.explanation: (d) Heart and soul- entire energy and effort. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute (replace) the bracketed segment in the following sentence. I look forward (see) you soon.
questions.explanation:
(b) to seeing
There are some phrases that are always followed by a
gerund(V ). Such phrases are ‘with a view to, looking forward to,
ing
in addition to, accustomed to, habituated to, be used to, prone to,
etc.’ Hence, ‘look forward to seeing’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Harish is clever than wise.
questions.explanation:
(d) more clever than
When we compare two qualities of the same person, the
comparative degree is formed by adding ‘more’, not by adding
‘-er’. Hence, ‘more clever than’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The firefighters tried their best to extinguish the fire.
questions.explanation: (c) Put out- to extinguish fire. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Research in Social Sciences is plagued nowadays on gloomy definitions and measurements.
questions.explanation:
(c) nowadays by gloomy definitions
‘By’ is used in passive voice to indicate the doer or agent of the
action. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘by’ has been used to
indicate the doer of the action ‘plagued’. Hence, ‘nowadays by
gloomy definitions’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Raghav, who studies tourism at present, is planning to go abroad after his graduation.
questions.explanation:
(d) is studying
Present continuous tense is used to indicate an action that is in
progress in the present. ‘Singular Subject + is + V ’ is the
ing
correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘is studying’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Placing a huge magnet atop the temple pose to being the biggest hurdle for the masons.
questions.explanation:
(d) posed to be
‘To + V ’, also known as infinitive, is the correct grammatical
1
structure. The given sentence is in the past tense, therefore, the
past form(V ) of the verb will be used. Hence, ‘posed to be’ is the
2
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: One of the most horrified serials of the Indian television industry was broadcast twenty years ago.
questions.explanation:
(a) most horrifying serials
‘Horrifying’ means causing a feeling of horror. The given
sentence states that one of the most horrifying serials of the
Indian television industry was broadcast twenty years ago.
Hence, ‘most horrifying serials’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Monika said to her mother that, "I have passed the examination."
options: Monika said to her mother that, "I am passed
Monika said to her mother, "I have passed
Monika said to her mother that, "she has passed
questions.explanation:
(b) Monika said to her mother, “I have passed
If the reported speech is given in inverted commas(“ ” ), it is
called direct speech. However, in the direct speech, we do not
use any conjunctions (‘that’, ‘if’, ‘whether’) after the reporting
verb (say). Therefore, ‘that’ will be removed from the given
sentence. Hence, option (b) is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If she had gone to the party, she could have met Amit.
questions.explanation:
(a) No substitution required.
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Heba dropped of the club unexpectedly to say hello and catch up.
questions.explanation:
(c) dropped by the club unexpectedly
The phrasal verb ‘drop by’ means to pay a brief casual visit. The
given sentence states that Heba dropped by the club
unexpectedly to say hello and catch up. Hence, ‘dropped by the
club unexpectedly’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Solving the riddle given by our teacher is farther beyond our capacity.
questions.explanation:
(d) far
Positive degree ‘far’ will be used in this sentence as there is no
comparison. Hence, ‘far’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Rohit Sharma is better than more other batsman in the world.
options: as good as the most other batsmen
questions.explanation:
(c) better than most other batsmen
‘More other’ must be replaced with ‘most other’, indicating the
majority of other batsmen. Plural noun is used with the adjective
‘other’. The given sentence states that Rohit Sharma is better
than the majority of other batsmen in the world. Hence, ‘better
than most other batsmen’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: There have been numerous attempts made by the citizens to restore parity.
questions.explanation:
(a) No substitution
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The given sentence has an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. India is not on war with Pakistan.
questions.explanation:
(c) not at
‘At war with’ is the correct phrase, which means to be in a
situation of war with an enemy nation. Hence, ‘not at’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The robbers stabbed him by a sharp knife and he started bleeding profusely on the spot.
questions.explanation:
(d) with a sharp knife
‘With’ is used when there is a physical contact between two
things. When a person is stabbed with a knife, the knife enters a
person’s body, indicating a physical contact. Hence, ‘with a sharp
knife’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The intersection of nature conservation and social justice is evident in efforts to ensure that marginalised communities and other backward classes should have equal access to natural reserves.
questions.explanation:
(c) apparent in endeavours to guarantee
‘Endeavour’ means an attempt to achieve a goal. ‘Guarantee’
means to ensure that something will happen. The phrase
‘evident in efforts to ensure’ means the same as ‘apparent in
endeavours to guarantee’. Hence, ‘apparent in endeavours to
guarantee’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I had to choose the best of the two options available.
questions.explanation:
(b) better of
‘Than’ is used when one thing is before the comparative degree
and the other comes afterwards. But when we talk about one out
of two, ‘of’ is used with comparative degree. The given sentence
talks about the one better option out of two options available.
Hence, ‘better of’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: After the heavy rains last Thursday, the water in the river raised another three feet.
questions.explanation:
(a) rose another three feet
‘Raised’ must be replaced with ‘rose’. ‘Raise’ means to cause
something to move upwards. ‘Rose’ means to go upwards or
higher. ‘Rose’ is the past form of ‘rise’, indicating simple past
tense. Hence, ‘rose another three feet’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Ramgopal is having a very big house in Mumbai.
questions.explanation:
(c) has
‘Have’ is a stative verb denoting possession. Stative verbs are
generally not used in the continuous tense. Rather, we use
simple present tense to talk about the present state. ‘Ramgopal’
is a singular subject that will take ‘has’ as a singular verb. Hence,
‘has’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I have never had and never will be dependent on him.
questions.explanation:
(c) never been
In the given sentence, the main verb is ‘be’. With ‘has/have/had’,
the third form of the verb is used. The first form of the verb is
used with modals (will, shall, can, may, might, could, would,
should, must). Hence, ‘never been(V )’ is the most appropriate
3
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Rahul was angry of his brother as he broke his pen.
questions.explanation:
(d) at
‘At’ is used with ‘angry’ for a person. ‘Angry at someone’ is the
correct phrase. Hence, ‘at’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The pineapple dessert was so delicious that we couldn’t help eat it.
options: so delicious that we couldn’t helping eat it
so that delicious we couldn’t help eating it
so delicious that we couldn’t help eating it
questions.explanation:
(d) so delicious that we couldn’t help eating it
The phrase “can’t help / couldn’t help” is used when you can not
resist doing something. Present participle(V ) is used after this
ing
phrase. Hence, “so delicious that we couldn’t help eating it” is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Autumn leaves shuffled beneath him as he wandered through the quiet forest.
questions.explanation:
(a) rustled underfoot
‘Rustle’ means to make a soft sound, as by moving leaves.
‘Underfoot’ means under your feet as you walk. The given
sentence states that autumn leaves rustled underfoot as he
wandered through the quiet forest. Hence, ‘rustled underfoot’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If we want to promote national integrity in our country, then we must desist our tendency of taking up with others.
questions.explanation:
(a) looking down upon
‘Taking up with’ must be replaced with the phrasal verb ‘looking
down upon’, which means to treat someone as unimportant or
not worthy of respect. The given sentence talks about desisting
the tendency of looking down upon others. Hence, ‘looking down
upon’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: .She confided in me on her anxious, whispering her secrets between sips of coffee.
questions.explanation:
(c) about her anxiety
Preposition ‘about’ is used to indicate the specific subject or
issue. We use a noun after any preposition. ‘Anxiety’ is the
correct noun to use here. ‘Anxiety’ means a feeling of worry,
nervousness or unease about something. Hence, ‘about her
anxiety’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: ‘Spy Family’ is a graphic novel that is a narrative work in which the story is conveyed to the reader using uninterrupted art in a traditional comics format.
questions.explanation:
(a) sequential art in a traditional ‘Sequential’ means in a
logical order. The given sentence states that ‘Spy Family’ is a
graphic novel that is a narrative work in which the story is
conveyed to the reader using sequential art in a traditional
comics format. Hence, 'sequential art in a traditional' is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She has been studying for two o’clock .
questions.explanation:
(b) studying since two o’clock
‘Since’ is used to indicate the point of time when something
started. Similarly, the given sentence states the time when she
started studying. Hence, “studying since two o’ clock” is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Spreading awareness about the rights of the consumers and the relief open to them in case they did not get their money’s worth of goods and service has rightly been identified as the first priority.
options: were unable to get their money’s worth
did not getting their money’s worth
will not get their money’s worth
questions.explanation:
(a) were unable to get their money’s worth
The phrase ‘did not get’ means to not be able to get something
in the past. ‘Unable’ means to not be able to do something.
Hence, “were unable to get their money’s worth” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Pollution levels have increased so largely that they are almost killing us.
questions.explanation:
(a) highly
‘Highly’ means at a high level. The given sentence states that
pollution levels have increased so highly that they are almost
killing us. Hence, 'highly' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. (Each participant have) performed well.
questions.explanation:
(b) Each participant has
‘Everyone/each/ every/ nothing/ everything/ anything/ either/
neither’ represents a singular noun. Therefore, singular verbs will
be used with them. Hence, ‘Each participant has’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: There are many factories in the operative area of the city.
questions.explanation:
(a) industrial
‘Industrial’ means having a lot of factories. The given sentence
states that there are many factories in the industrial area of the
city. Hence, 'industrial' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I have been living in Hyderabad since I am born .
questions.explanation:
(d) since I was born
‘Since’ is used to indicate the point of time in the past when
something began. Therefore, past tense will be used in the
clause beginning with ‘since’. Hence, ‘since I was born’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Rare species of frogs were very quicker identified by Stella.
questions.explanation:
(b) of frogs were very quickly
The given sentence needs an adverb ‘quickly’ to modify the verb
‘identified’, not an adjective ‘quicker’. Hence, ‘of frogs were very
quickly’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He was an irresponsible person to the matter of taking up responsibilities.
options: at the matter of taking up
in the matter of taking up
by the matter of taking up
along the matter of taking up
questions.explanation:
(b) in the matter of taking up
‘In’ is used to indicate a specific situation or circumstance. The
given passage states that he was an irresponsible person in the
matter of taking up responsibilities. Hence, 'in the matter of
taking up' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Mayra has the ability for mathematics.
questions.explanation:
(c) Aptitude
‘Aptitude’ means a natural ability to do something. The given
sentence states that Mayra has the aptitude for mathematics.
Hence, 'aptitude' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. They could (always) stay in, or go for a walk.
questions.explanation:
(c) either
‘Either…or’ is a fixed pair of conjunctions. Hence, ‘either’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Charles Darwin is renowned for his book on evolution, ‘On the Origin of Species’, which laid down a treasure ofsubstantiation that evolution occurs, and projected a mechanism, that is, natural selection, for how it does so.
options: laid into a treasure of substantiation
laid about a treasure of substantiation
laid away a treasure of substantiation
laid out a treasure of substantiation
questions.explanation:
(d) laid out a treasure of substantiation
‘Laid out’ means explained or described something in a clear
and detailed way. The given sentence states that Charles Darwin
is renowned for his book on evolution, ‘On the Origin of Species’,
which laid down a treasure of substantiation that evolution
occurs. Hence, ‘laid out a treasure of substantiation’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Our legal system must frame proper legal rules for juvenile criminals.
questions.explanation:
(d) young
The given sentence states that our legal system must frame
legal rules for young criminals. Hence, ‘young’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The programme on TV was now shown the blurring faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre.
options: were now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre.
was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre
were now showing the blurring faces of the inmates from the rehabilitation centre
was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates upon the rehabilitation centre
questions.explanation:
(b) was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates
of the rehabilitation centre
‘Singular Sub. + was + V ing’ is grammatically the correct structure
for a sentence which is in the past continuous tense. Hence,
‘was now showing(V ) the blurred faces of the inmates of the
ing
rehabilitation centre’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: When I saw him, I will ask him to return the book he borrowed.
questions.explanation:
(d) see him
If ‘when’ is used to denote the time of a future event, it is used in
simple present tense. First form of the verb is used with pronoun
‘I’ in the simple present tense. Hence, ‘see(V 1) him’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Gourav was no good than a foolish person.
questions.explanation:
(a) no better
We use comparative degree with ‘than’ to make comparison.
However, ‘better’ is the comparative degree of ‘good’. Hence, ‘no
better’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If I was the queen, I would give a handsome sum towards education.
questions.explanation:
(b) were the queen
The phrase ‘If i were’ is generally used in the subjunctive mood
to talk about possibilities, wishes, or conditions that are contrary
to reality. ‘If I were… (would + V ) / (would have + V )’ is the
1 3
correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘If I were the queen’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Five years later, I was eating this same dish at the same restaurant.
questions.explanation:
(c) am eating
The given sentence implies that the person ate a dish at a
restaurant and five years later, he is eating the same dish at the
same restaurant. Therefore, the sentence will be written in
simple present tense. Hence, ‘am eating’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Beyond skills, experience, and training, companies search for applicants who display excitement — those they believe shall carry out allocated responsibilities cheerfully and cooperatively.
options: shall take up any designated obligations
should pick up all skills and works
questions.explanation:
(b) will execute assigned duties
‘Execute’ means to carry out fully. ‘Duties’ means responsibility.
The given sentence states that beyond skills, experience, and
training, companies search for applicants who display
excitement — those they believe will execute assigned duties
cheerfully and cooperatively. Hence, ‘will execute assigned
duties’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The mother asked the child, “Will you tell me who did accompany you to the airport?”
questions.explanation:
(c) who accompanied you
When a question is part of a sentence, the helping verb is written
after the subject, not before the subject. Past form (V 2 ) is used
in simple past tense. Hence, ‘who accompanied(V 2 ) you’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Satya is always great to his friends who helped him when he was in trouble.
questions.explanation:
(d) grateful
‘Grateful’ means showing appreciation for something done. The
given sentence states that Satya is always grateful to his friends
who helped him when he was in trouble. Hence, ‘grateful’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The team always anticipate a bowling friendly pitch on their easy victory in the T20 matches.
questions.explanation:
(b) pitch for their easy victory
‘For’ is used to indicate the purpose or reason for something.
Similarly, the team anticipate a bowling friendly pitch for the
purpose of easy victory in the T20 matches. Hence, ‘pitch for
their easy victory’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The wedding was put on until January.
questions.explanation:
(b) put off
The phrasal verb ‘put off’ means to delay something until a later
time. The given sentence states that the wedding was put off
until January. Hence, ‘put off’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Everyone called the reporter a daredevil after he came back safely from the war zone.
questions.explanation: (b) A daredevil- a fearless person. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Carnatic music is usually performed by a small troupe of actors, consisting of a principal performer, a melodic accompaniment, and a rhythm accompaniment.
questions.explanation:
(b) ensemble of musicians
‘Ensemble’ means a group of musicians, dancers, or actors who
perform together. The given sentence talks about carnatic
music, so the correct phrase to use is ‘ensemble of musicians’.
Hence, ‘ensemble of musicians’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: It is very hard for her to provide the necessities of her family.
questions.explanation:
(a) the necessities to her family
‘To’ is used to indicate the receiver of an action or object. In the
given sentence, ‘her family’ is the receiver of the necessities.
Hence, ‘the necessities to her family’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: To the general public, William was best known as a crusader for peace and as an admired critic about social, political and ethical subjects.
options: for peace and as an admired critic by
for peace and as an admired critic on
about peace and as an admired critic about
in peace and as an admired critic about
questions.explanation:
(b) for peace and as an admired critic on
‘On’ is generally used to indicate the topic or subject of
discussion. Hence, ‘on’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: No matter how hard work you, your boss will not recognise your efforts.
questions.explanation:
(a) hard you work
‘Subject + main verb’ is the correct order for the sentence. ‘You’
is the subject and ‘work’ is its main verb. Hence, ‘hard you work’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: As the rulers of the planet, humans like to think that it is the largest creatures that will emerge victorious from the struggle for survival.
options: it is the most large creatures
questions.explanation:
(d) they are the largest creatures
‘Humans’ is a plural noun that will take the plural pronoun ‘they’
and the plural verb ‘are’. Hence, ‘they are the largest creatures’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Experts acknowledged that some counterfeiting of document techniques are virtually impossible to detect.
questions.explanation:
(b) forgery
‘Forgery’ means the crime of illegally copying something in order
to deceive someone. The given sentence states that experts
acknowledged that some forgery techniques are virtually
impossible to detect. Hence, ‘forgery’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If it had not rained, they would not postpone the programmes.
questions.explanation:
(c) would not have postponed
The given sentence is an example of a third conditional
sentence and the correct grammatical structure for it is “If +
past perfect (had + V )…….. Would have + V ”. Hence, ‘would not
3 3
have postponed’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Sivamani is working as an electrician for the past 22 years.
questions.explanation:
(b) has been working
Perfect continuous tense is used when the time period is given
with ‘for/since’. ‘Singular subject + has been + V ing’ is the correct
grammatical structure for this sentence. Hence, ‘has been
working’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Her thinning grey hair was hanging on her bony forehead.
questions.explanation:
(c) straggling over
‘Straggling over’ means spread out in an irregular way. The given
sentence states that her thinning grey hair was spread out
irregularly over her bony forehead. Hence, ‘straggling over’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: An intense wish to learn something keeps the nerves active.
questions.explanation:
(a) powerful
‘Intense’ means the same as powerful. The given sentence
states that a powerful wish to learn something keeps the nerves
active. Hence, ‘powerful’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Rohan exercised and ate a lot, lest he should not be weak.
options: lest he would not be weak.
questions.explanation:
(d) lest he should be weak
‘Not’ will be removed as the use of ‘not’ with ‘lest’ is superfluous.
Hence, ‘lest he should be weak’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Bankrupts are those who are incapable to pay their debts
questions.explanation:
(c) incompetent
‘Incompetent’ means incapable of doing something. The given
sentence states that bankrupts are those who are incompetent
to pay their debts. Hence, ‘incompetent’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. He (seek) for the wallet in his pocket.
questions.explanation:
(a) Sought
‘Sought’ is the correct verb to use here. ‘Sought’ is the past form
of ‘seek’, indicating simple past tense. Hence, ‘sought’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Do you know where does she reside ?
questions.explanation:
(c) where she resides?
When a question is a part of a sentence, the correct structure is
“Wh. word + Subject + verb”. ‘She’ is a singular subject that will
take the singular verb ‘resides’. Hence, ‘where she resides?’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: A computer can’t function without it’s mother board.
questions.explanation:
(a) its
‘Its’ is a possessive used for things. Here, ‘its’ has been used for
a computer. Hence, ‘its’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Transnational linkages, for example, sever the nation-state’s integrity and corrupt state-society relations.
questions.explanation:
(a) cohesion and erode
‘Cohesion’ means forming a united whole & ‘erode’ means
gradually destroy. The given sentence states that transnational
linkages, for example, sever the nation-state’s cohesion and
erode state-society relations. Hence, ‘cohesion and erode’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: His house is smaller than you .
questions.explanation:
(a) is smaller than yours
The comparison is between two houses, not the house and
person. So, we will use a possessive pronoun ‘yours’ instead of
‘you’. Hence, ‘is smaller than yours’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She was foolish enough to think that she be completely safe now.
questions.explanation:
(c) is completely safe
The use of the adverb ‘now’ indicates present tense and the
present tense form of ‘be’ is ‘is’ for the singular subject (she).
Hence, ‘is completely safe’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: No sooner did Mr. Piyahri Mishra finish his chemistry lecture that the students began to leave.
options: so the students began to leave.
then the students began to leave.
and the students began to leave.
than the students began to leave.
questions.explanation:
(d) than the students began to leave.
‘No sooner …than’ is a fixed pair of conjunctions. Therefore, ‘that’
will be replaced with ‘than’. Hence, ‘than the students began to
leave’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Sanat has just arrived in Mysore on transfer; he requests his friend Raghu to help him find an appropriate location.
questions.explanation:
(b) a rented accommodation
‘Rented accommodation’ means a property that is occupied by a
tenant who pays rent to the owner, or landlord. The given
sentence states that he requests his friend Raghu to help him
find a rented accommodation. Hence, 'a rented accommodation'
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: This book giving us much information about our freedom fighters who lost their lives while serving our motherland.
questions.explanation:
(d) gives us much information
According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular
subject always takes a singular verb. At the end of a singular
verb, s/es is used. In the given sentence, ‘this book’ is a singular
subject that will take ‘gives’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘gives us
much information’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous decade, chiefly because of a boost in Coeliac and Crohn’s disease cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious clients.
options: pretty much entirely because of a boil-down
questions.explanation:
(d) owing primarily to a rise
‘Owing to’ means because of & ‘primarily’ means mainly. ‘Rise’
means increase in number. The given sentence states that the
food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous
decade, owing primarily to a rise in Coeliac and Crohn’s disease
cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious
clients. Hence, ‘owing primarily to a rise’ is the most appropriate
answer.
Questions (286 to 376) (Correct)

questions.prompt: Aesthetic value is specifically a way in which we can get positive conclude value from the world at large.
questions.explanation:
(c) can get positive conclusive value
The given sentence needs an adjective (conclusive) to describe
the noun ‘value’, and not the verb ‘conclude’. Hence, ‘can get
positive conclusive value’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Ranjith failed in all his exams as he had been addicted of social media.
options: as he had been addicted at
as he had been addicted on
as he had been addicted in
as he had been addicted to
questions.explanation:
(d) as he had been addicted to
‘To’ is a fixed preposition used after the verb ‘addicted’. Hence,
‘as he had been addicted to’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The cynical investors believed in every word the analysts said.
questions.explanation:
(a) credulous
‘Credulous’ means willing to believe or trust too readily. The
given sentence states that the credulous investors believed in
every word the analysts said. Hence, 'credulous' is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: It is nothing else your pride which makes you say such a thing.
options: else but your pride which make
else but your pride which makes
questions.explanation:
(d) else but your pride which makes
‘Nothing … but’ or ‘Nothing else … but’ means only. The given
sentence needs the conjunction ‘but’ after ‘nothing else’ to make
it grammatically correct. Hence, ‘else but your pride which
makes’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Mr. Adhil called back but he wasn’t able to find the scooter part he needed.
options: called down but he wasn’t able to
called off but he wasn’t able to
called around but he wasn’t able to
called up to but he wasn’t able to
questions.explanation:
(c) called around but he wasn’t able to
‘Call around’ means to call multiple people to find information
about something. The given sentence states that Mr. Adhil
called around but he wasn’t able to find the scooter part he
needed. Hence, 'called around but he wasn’t able to' is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. We need to _____ a solution to this problem before it gets worse.
questions.explanation:
(d) come up with
‘Come up with’ means to suggest or think of an idea or plan. The
given sentence states that we need to come up with a solution
to this problem before it gets worse. Hence, 'come up with' is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Nina has not yet learned how to straighten up and fly right.
options: forget the wrongdoings of the others
improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously
be professional in flying the aircraft
remember the past and prepare for the future
questions.explanation:
(b) improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously
The phrase ‘straighten up and fly right’ means to get serious and
stop acting absurd anymore. The given sentence states that
Nina has not yet learned how to improve her absurd behaviour
and act seriously. Hence, 'improve her absurd behaviour and act
seriously' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I had not only helped her by giving hints but also with providing her links.
questions.explanation:
(a) helped her not only by
The same part of speech is used after pair conjunctions such as
‘not only…but also’. There is a preposition followed by
gerund(providing) after ‘but also’. Therefore, ‘not only’ will be
placed before the preposition ‘by’. Hence, ‘helped her not only by’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Positive self-talk have a great affect on one’s self-worth.
questions.explanation:
(d) has a great effect
According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular
subject always takes a singular verb. In the given sentence,
‘positive self-talk’ is a singular subject that will take ‘has’ as a
singular verb. Also, the adjective ‘great’ needs a noun to qualify
its meaning. Hence, ‘has a great effect’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Arushya purchased the most good of all the suits kept in the shop.
questions.explanation:
(b) the best
‘Best’ is the correct superlative degree of ‘good’. Hence, ‘the
best’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Even if you’ve never heard his name, you’ve probably met someone with his words tattooed in their skin or heard them sung at a music concert.
questions.explanation:
(d) tattooed on their skin
‘On’ is used to indicate the surface in contact with the object.
Similarly, the tattoo lies on the surface of the skin. Hence,
‘tattooed on their skin’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. If he runs, he (get) there in time.
questions.explanation:
(a) will get
The given sentence is an example of the first conditional
sentence and the correct grammatical structure is “if + simple
present…….will +V 1 ”. Hence ‘will get(V 1 )’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Ashoka was the greatest than all the Mauryan Emperors .
questions.explanation:
(b) of the Mauryan Emperors
‘Than’ is used with comparative degree while ‘of’ is used after
the superlative degree. ‘The + superlative adjective + of + plural
noun/pronoun’ is the correct structure. Hence, 'of the Mauryan
Emperors' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. I said I (don't) understand.
questions.explanation:
(c) didn't
The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb
of past tense. ‘Did’ is a helping verb of simple past tense. Hence,
didn’t is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I picked up my little clock and it began to dance gracefully.
questions.explanation:
(c) chime prettily
‘Chime’ means (of a bell or clock) make melodious ringing
sounds. The given passage states that I picked up my little clock
and it began to chime prettily. Hence, ‘chime prettily’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The chair I have bought recently is costly than what I bought last year.
questions.explanation:
(b) is costlier
We use a comparative degree with ‘than’ to make a comparison
between two things. ‘Costlier’ is the correct comparative degree
of ‘costly’. Hence, ‘is costlier’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: RN Right’s literary works helped redefine discussions in race relations in America in the mid-20th century.
questions.explanation:
(d) of race relations in America
‘Of’ means relating to something. The given sentence states that
RN Right’s literary works helped redefine discussions of race
relations in America in the mid-20th century. Hence, 'of race
relations in America' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.explanation:
(d) that enable the hair to grow
'That' is a relative pronoun used to introduce a relative clause,
which provides additional information about a noun. Here, the
clause provides additional information about the ingredients.
Hence, ‘that enable the hair to grow’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She argued against the unnecessary split in the committee.
questions.explanation: (c) Split - division. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Had you been to Dubai, I would also go with you.
questions.explanation:
(c) I would have gone
The given sentence is an example of a third conditional
sentence and the correct grammatical structure for it is “had +
Subject + been …….. would have + V 3”. Hence, ‘I would have
gone(V 3)’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the word segment from the options that can substitute the bracketed word segment meaningfully. Telangana artists (are know for the amazing bronze castings).
options: Have been knew to the amazing bronze castings
Are known for their amazing bronze castings
Is known to the amazing bronze castings
Have to know the amazing bronze castings
questions.explanation:
(b) are known for their amazing bronze castings
The given sentence is a passive voice of simple present tense
and the subject ‘Telangana artists’ is plural. ‘Plural Subject + are
+ V 3’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘are
known for the amazing bronze castings’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: It has been found that the trees are being destroyed by a moth.
questions.explanation:
(c) No substitution required
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: No sooner did we reach at the party that it began to rain.
questions.explanation:
(d) than it began to rain
‘That’ must be replaced by ‘than’. ‘No sooner…than’ is a fixed
conjunction pair. Hence, ‘than it began to rain’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The interdisciplinary approach utilised in this study facilitates comprehensive understanding of the complex phenomenon under investigation.
options: will have facilitated a comprehensive understanding
questions.explanation:
(d) facilitated a comprehensive understanding
The given sentence is in the simple past tense, so the verb must
be used in the simple past form(V 2). Hence, ‘facilitated(V 2) a
comprehensive understanding’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He passed away in the year 1950 at 10 a.m. on 13 July.
options: in the year 1950 at 10 a.m. on 13 July
on 13 July at 10 a.m. in the year 1950
at 10 a.m. on 13 July in the year 1950
in the year 1950 on 13 July at 10 a.m.
questions.explanation:
(c) at 10 a.m. on 13 July in the year 1950
The correct order is time followed by day, month and then the
year. Hence, ‘at 10 a.m. on 13 July in the year 1950’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I was in Oman around two months.
questions.explanation:
(d) for
‘Around’ must be replaced with ‘for’ as ‘for’ is used to indicate a
period of time. Hence, ‘for two months’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The meeting closed with a vote of thanks.
questions.explanation:
(d) concluded
‘Concluded’ means to bring something to an end or finish,
particularly in a formal context. The given sentence states that
the meeting concluded with a vote of thanks. Hence, ‘concluded’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: At his wit’s end, he decided to return to his parents as he was unable to cope up with the stress of adjusting at a new place.
questions.explanation: (c) At his wit’s end- not knowing what to do. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Peter was the last to know that she had been cheating of him
questions.explanation:
(c) cheating on him
There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. ‘Cheat on
someone’ is the correct phrase. Hence, 'cheating on him' is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The film was made in Botswana, whose wildlife parks is larger to those in Kenya.
questions.explanation:
(c) are larger than
‘Wildlife parks’ is a plural subject that will take ‘are’ as a plural
verb. ‘Than’ is used with a comparative degree to make a
comparison. Hence, ‘are larger than’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I opened the box beneath the table and took of a book, the Materia Medica.
questions.explanation:
(d) took out
The phrasal verb ‘take out’ means to remove something from
somewhere. The given sentence states that I opened the box
and took out a book, the Materia Medica. Hence, ‘took out’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Do not later about the street.
questions.explanation:
(b) loiter around
The correct phrase is ‘loiter around’ which means to hang
around or stay in an area without any specific purpose. Hence,
‘loiter around’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The experienced surgeon handled the delicate procedure with care and precision.
questions.explanation:
(c) seasoned
‘Experienced’ must be replaced with ‘seasoned’ which means
highly experienced and skilled, especially after many years of
practice. The given sentence states that the seasoned surgeon
handled the delicate procedure with care and precision. Hence,
‘seasoned’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Planning to go for a movie just before the final-year examination is nothing but skating on thin ice.
questions.explanation: (d) Skating on thin ice - being in a risky situation. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Shakespeare is greater than any other English poet.
questions.explanation:
(b) was greater than
‘Shakespeare’ is a late (not alive) English poet. So, we need to
use the past form(V 2 ) of the verb to indicate the simple past
tense. Hence, ‘was greater than’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I prefer walking than riding.
questions.explanation:
(d) walking to riding
‘To’ is a fixed preposition used after the verb ‘prefer’. Hence,
‘walking to riding’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Youth is the time when the seeds of character is sown.
options: the seeds of character had been sown
the seeds of character were sown
the seeds of character will have been sowing
the seeds of character are sown
questions.explanation:
(d) the seeds of character are sown
According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a plural subject
always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘seeds’ is a
plural subject that will take ‘are’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘the
seeds of character are sown’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: An awkward neither grammatically accurate sentence is the result of centre implanting.
questions.explanation:
(d) awkward but grammatically
‘But’ is used to indicate a contrasting idea. Similarly, the word
‘awkward’ contrasts with the idea ‘grammatically accurate’.
Hence, ‘awkward but grammatically’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The referee declared that the participant who will score the highest points in the tally will take away the cash prize of ₹50 lakh.
options: who can score the highest point
who could score the highest point
who settles scores the highest point
questions.explanation:
(c) who scores the highest point
‘Scoring the highest points’ is a general rule or condition for
taking away the cash prize of ₹50 lakh. Simple present tense is
used to state a general truth or condition. ‘Singular Sub. +
V 1 -s/es’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘who
scores the highest point’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: My friends are on a trip to the world.
questions.explanation:
(b) around the world
‘To’ is used for a fixed or particular location. Whereas ‘around’ is
used with ‘world’. Hence, ‘around the world’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The Government must strive to provide a/an fair and square deal to the citizen of its country.
questions.explanation: (b) Fair and square- honest and straightforward. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The culprit had been shot from the back by the police inspector.
questions.explanation:
(c) in
Here, ‘in’ will be used to indicate that the bullet that was shot by
the police inspector hit the back of the culprit. Hence, ‘in’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Though Kalpana listened to Sheetal carefully, she knew that she should take it with a grain of salt.
options: regard it as exaggerated and not completely true
be do it meticulously as taking salt
accept it as really useful and worthy
questions.explanation:
(a) Take it with a grain of salt- regard it as exaggerated
and not completely true. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The author’s writing style is characterised by its poetic language.
questions.explanation:
(d) lyrical language
‘Lyrical’ means poetic and romantic. The given sentence states
that the author’s writing style is characterised by its poetic
language. Hence, ‘lyrical language’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Read the books of APJ Abdul Kalam, who was a scholar.
questions.explanation: (d) A man of letters - a scholar. (Correct)

questions.prompt: My friend vanished when the goons came to fight with me.
questions.explanation:
(c) disappeared when the thugs arrived
‘Vanish’ means to disappear suddenly and completely. ‘Goon’
means a thug hired to commit acts of violence or intimidation.
Hence, ‘disappeared when the thugs came’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If I was very rich, I would spend all my time and money for the poor.
questions.explanation:
(d) If I were very rich
The phrase ‘If I were’ is used to refer to an imaginary situation. ‘If
I were … would + V ’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence,
1
‘If I were very rich’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Last night, I failed to sleep because of some familiar issues that couldn't be avoided.
questions.explanation: (b) Inevitable - a situation which cannot be avoided. (Correct)

questions.prompt: No sooner had she finished her breakfast that she had received a phone call from her boss, informing her that she needed to come to work immediately.
questions.explanation:
(b) than she received
‘No sooner…than’ is a fixed conjunction pair. If there are two
actions in the past, the 1st action is written in past perfect tense
(had + V 3) and the 2nd action is written in simple past tense(V 2).
Hence, ‘than she received(V 2)’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: After he leave, we discussed his suggestion.
questions.explanation:
(c) he had left
If two actions happened in the past, 1st action is written in past
perfect tense(had + V 3 ) and 2nd action is written in simple past
tense(V 2 ). The action of leaving happened first. Hence, ‘he had
left(V 3 )’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Though very informative, Shweta's article was mercilessly rejected of the editor.
questions.explanation:
(a) was mercilessly rejected by
‘By’ is used in passive voice to indicate the doer of the action.
Similarly, ‘editor’ is the doer of the action of rejecting. Hence,
‘was mercilessly rejected by’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Mathew decided to complete the marathon to prove that he is still fit as a fiddle in his eighties.
options: an owner of a fit horse
questions.explanation: (b) Fit as a fiddle - a fit and energetic person (Correct)

questions.prompt: My son will carry out my business in my absence.
questions.explanation:
(b) carry on
‘Carry on’ means to continue a task or an activity. The given
sentence states that my son will carry on my business in my
absence. Hence, ‘carry on’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: It is a fact that the same judgement can often be taken by more than one way.
questions.explanation:
(a) be taken in more than
The phrasal verb ‘take in’ means to understand something that
you read or hear. The given sentence states that it is a fact that
the same judgement can be taken in more than one way. Hence,
‘be taken in more than’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The company plans to expand its business to the international market.
questions.explanation:
(d) to increase
‘Expand’ means to increase the extent or scope of something.
The given sentence states that the company plans to increase
its business to the international market. Hence, ‘to increase’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He always used to say that he was not a beggar by choice and if someone could employ him, he would like to eat.
questions.explanation:
(c) love to work
The given sentence talks about a person who is not a beggar by
choice. This means he would love to work if somebody could
employ him. Hence, ‘love to work’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The manager, decided at last to bring the stenographer to book for her illegal money transactions after trying to ignore it several times.
options: bring her for a detailed investigation
make her accountable for her conduct
place her in a safe supportive position
questions.explanation:
(c) make her accountable for her conduct
‘Bring someone to book’ is an idiom which means to hold
someone accountable for something they have done. Hence,
‘make her accountable for her conduct’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: In yesterday’s fire accident, her feets are burnt badly.
questions.explanation:
(b) her feet were
‘Yesterday’ indicates past tense. ‘Feets’ is incorrect as ‘feet’ is
the correct plural form of ‘foot’. Hence, ‘her feet were’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the most appropriate option with correct usage of the preposition to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The Centre of Excellence for Data Analytics (CEDA) provides quality data analytic services to various government departments on all levels as well as to public sector units at the Centre and in states.
options: various government departments at all levels
various government departments from all levels
various government departments in all levels
various government departments through all levels
questions.explanation:
(a) various government departments at all levels
‘At’ is used to indicate the position, rank or level of something.
Hence, ‘various government departments at all levels’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: You have tears, prepare to shed them now.
questions.explanation:
(d) If you have tears
‘If’ is used to provide the condition under which something
happens. Similarly, in the given sentence, having tears is the
condition for shedding tears. Hence, ‘If you have tears’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence Meaningfully. The minister promised to provide free laptops to the public if his (party came in power).
questions.explanation:
(c) party forms the government
‘To come into power’ means to form the government. The given
sentence states that the minister promised to provide free
laptops to the public if his party forms the government. Hence,
‘party forms the government’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: This is the group of leaders in whom the ruling government has placed its trust.
questions.explanation:
(a) no substitution
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: During the preparation for competitive exams, Meena avoided going to parties.
questions.explanation:
(a) steered clear of
The phrase ‘steer clear of’ means to deliberately avoid
something. Hence, ‘steered clear of’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The woman to who I sold my house was a criminal.
questions.explanation:
(c) to whom I sold
‘To’ is a preposition and we generally use an objective case
pronoun after any preposition. Therefore, ‘who’ must be replaced
with ‘whom’. Hence, ‘to whom I sold’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: A sharp fall in the price of jute have led the poor jute farmers to the brink of starvation.
options: have lead the poor jute farmers
has led the poor jute farmers
questions.explanation:
(d) has led the poor jute farmers
According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular
subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always
takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘A sharp fall’ is a
singular subject that will take ‘has’ as a singular verb. Hence,
‘has led the poor jute farmers’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: We should not underestimate the signification of female education.
questions.explanation:
(c) underestimate the significance
‘Significance’ is the correct word to use here. ‘Significance’
means importance or meaningfulness. The given sentence
states that we should not underestimate the significance of
female education. Hence, ‘underestimate the significance’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Half of the property given to his sons by the businessman last year.
options: Half of the property has been given
Half of the property was given
Half of the property is given
questions.explanation:
(b) Half of the property was given
The given sentence is in the passive voice as the doer of the
action is given after the preposition ‘by’. The phrase ‘last year’
indicates simple past tense. ‘Singular Sub. + was + V ’ is the
3
correct grammatical structure for the passive voice of simple
past tense. Hence, ‘Half of the property was given(V )’ is the
3
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Even after becoming bankrupt, Charlie is able to maintain an outward show.
questions.explanation:
(d) Keep up appearance- maintain an outward show.
E.g.- Even though he was worried, he kept up appearances and
smiled. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Amit is also a chip off the old block like his brother, Tandon.
options: resembling his parents in character and appearance
talking to others tough like a stone
getting ready for the future endeavours
questions.explanation:
(a) chip off the old block- resembling his parents in
character and appearance. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Reena decided not to go to work today because she was feeling sick.
questions.explanation: (d) Under the weather- feeling sick. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He wanted to visiting the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
questions.explanation:
(b) wanted to visit
‘To + V 1 ’ , also known as an infinitive, is the correct grammatical
structure. Hence, ‘wanted to visit(V 1)’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: His interpretation of the facts was impressive.
questions.explanation:
(c) understanding of realities
We generally use a noun, pronoun or a gerund(V ) as the
ing
subject of a sentence. Hence, ‘understanding(V ing ) of realities’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

have + V ’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Therefore,

‘should’ must be replaced with ‘would’. Hence, ‘I would have
made(V )’ is the most appropriate answer.
3 (Correct)

questions.prompt: What exactly have the teachers being doing wrong ?
questions.explanation:
(c) teachers been doing
‘Have been + V ing’ is the correct grammatical structure for the
sentence which is in the present perfect continuous tense.
Hence, ‘teachers been doing(V ing)’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If his father will give money, he will buy a sports bike.
questions.explanation:
(a) If his father gives money
The given sentence is an example of the first conditional
sentence and ‘if + Simple Present Tense… will + V ’ is the correct

grammatical structure for it. ‘Father’ is a singular subject that
will take ‘gives’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘If his father gives
money’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I have been living without a lot of money since I lost my job.
options: as genuine as a three-dollar bill
questions.explanation: (a) living hand to mouth- living without a lot of money. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The road is too busy for elderly people that they cannot cross safely.
options: that it is impossible for them to cross
that it cannot be crossed properly.
that it is difficult to cross.
questions.explanation:
(b) to cross safely
‘Too + adjective/ adverb + to + V ’ is the correct grammatical
1
structure. Hence, ‘to cross(V ) safely’ is the most appropriate
1
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the most appropriate option with correct usage of the preposition to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The core part in Artificial Intelligence (AI) is knowledge engineering, machine learning, machine perception, and robotics.
options: The core part from Artificial Intelligence
The core part with Artificial Intelligence
The core part of Artificial Intelligence
The core part on Artificial Intelligence
questions.explanation:
(c) The core part of Artificial Intelligence ‘Of’ is used to
indicate a part or component of something. The given sentence
talks about the core part of Artificial Intelligence. Hence, ‘The
core part of Artificial intelligence’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The veteran footballer was expected for reach here by 10 o’clock, the notice said.
questions.explanation:
(a) expected to reach here
There are some verbs that are followed by an infinitive(to + V 1).
These verbs are ‘agree, decide, appear, expect, fail, afford, wish,
aim, etc’. Hence, ‘expected to reach(V ) here’ is the most
1
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Mr. Patel is likely to win the elections in the sweeping majority.
questions.explanation:
(d) elections by a sweeping majority
‘By’ is used to indicate the amount or extent of something. In the
given sentence, ‘by’ has been used to indicate the amount of
majority in the elections. Hence, ‘elections by a sweeping
majority’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Not a word didn’t they speak to the others about the sad turn of events.
questions.explanation:
(a) did they speak
The given sentence talks about the sad turn of events in the
past. ‘Did + V 1’ is the correct grammatical structure for the
sentence which is in the simple past tense. Hence, ‘did they
speak(V 1 )’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Before she began, she asked the teacher whether she write with a pen or a pencil.
questions.explanation:
(c) she should write
‘Should’ is used to indicate what is probable. Pen and pencil are
probable ways to write. Hence, ‘she should write’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The Sumo wrestler seemed to be incapable in being tired.
questions.explanation:
(c) incapable of being tired
‘Of’ is a fixed preposition used after ‘capable / incapable’. Hence,
‘incapable of being fired’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: My grandmother helps us in all the problems. She has a remedy for all the diseases.
questions.explanation:
(b) Panacea - a remedy for all the diseases.
Service- the occupation or function of serving.
Fanatic- a person who is extremely interested in something.
Heretic- a person whose religious beliefs are believed to be
wrong or evil. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He is feeding a male dog and female dog
options: a male dog and lady dog
questions.explanation:
(c) a dog and a bitch
A female dog is called a bitch. Hence, ‘a dog and a bitch’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: What flavour ice cream do you want?
questions.explanation:
(d) flavour of ice cream
‘Of’ is used to show one thing related to another. Similarly,
flavour is related to ice cream. Hence, ‘flavour of ice cream’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The quality of students of an educational institute is of great importance and a crucial starting point
options: The quality of students in an educational institute is in great importance and a crucial starting point.
The quality of students in an educational institute is of great importance and is a crucial start point
The quality of students in an educational institute is of great importance and a crucial starting point.

of great importance and a crucial starting point.
