replaced with ‘students in an educational institute’. We generally
use the preposition ‘in’ to indicate the presence or location of
something inside something else. The given sentence talks
about the quality of students present in an educational institute.
Hence, option (d) is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The serenity of the river was a sight to behold.
questions.explanation:
(d) pleasant to see
The phrase ‘a sight to behold’ means a person is extremely
pleased to see it. Hence, ‘pleasant to see’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Inspite mother’s milk is vital to a child’s health, a number of FMCG companies wrongly advertise artificially prepared infant formulas as being the best for the child.
questions.explanation:
(b) Though mother’s milk
‘Though’ is used to express contrast between two ideas. The
given sentence states that mother’s milk is vital to a child's
health, which contrasts with the advertisement of artificially
prepared infant formulas. Hence, “Though mother’s milk” is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She asked me where my hometown is and where I worked.
questions.explanation:
(b) hometown was
The given sentence is in the past tense, therefore, we will use the
helping verb of past tense. ‘Is’ must be replaced with ‘was’.
Hence, ‘hometown was’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Ice melts fastly in the sun.
questions.explanation:
(c) melts fast
‘Fastly’ is an incorrect word. ‘Fast’ is an adverb which modifies
the verb ‘melts’. Hence, ‘melts fast’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: All the kith and kin of my deceased landlady were present to attend her funeral.
questions.explanation: (b) Kith and kin - blood relatives. (Correct)

questions.prompt: You have hurt so many people. Now, it is time to get a taste of your own medicine.
options: to be treated the way you have treated others
to be in a risky situation
to lose control in a situation
to benefit from two different opportunities .
questions.explanation:
(a) To get a taste of your own medicine- to be treated
the way you have treated others. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what is expected out of me.
options: avoiding to talk about the issue
questions.explanation:
(c) Beating around the bush- avoiding to talk about the
issue. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I have been yet to go to the flower exhibition at Delhi University.
questions.explanation:
(d) have yet
The given sentence is in the active voice as the subject ‘I’ is the
being considered the doer of the action. Therefore, ‘been’ will be
removed from the sentence. ‘Have to’ is a semi-modal and takes
the first form of the verb(go) after it. Hence, ‘have yet’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the option that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the following sentence meaningfully. You all need to (get into) the books prescribed in your syllabus.
questions.explanation:
(c) go through
‘Go through’ is a phrasal verb which means to study something
in detail. The given sentence states that you all need to go
through the books prescribed in your syllabus. Hence, ‘go
through’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She faced a session of abuse after insisting that she was too beautiful to be liked.
questions.explanation:
(b) tirade of abuse
‘Tirade of abuse’ is the correct phrase to use here. It means a
long angry speech in which someone criticies a person. The
given sentence states that she faced a tirade of abuse after
insisting that she was too beautiful to be liked. Hence, ‘tirade of
abuse’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: This secret will remain between you and I.
questions.explanation:
(d) between you and me
A preposition takes an objective case pronoun after it. ‘Between’
is a preposition that will take ‘me’ instead of ‘I’. Hence, ‘between
you and me’ is the most appropriate answer.
Questions (468 to 558) (Correct)

questions.prompt: The plot of the story effects the character and their growth.
questions.explanation:
(b) affects the character
The given sentence needs a verb, not the noun ‘effects’ for the
subject ‘the plot of the story’. ‘The plot of the story’ is a singular
subject that will take ‘affects’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘affects
the character’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The enigma of quantum mechanics remains inscrutably elusive despite of decades of intensive research by the world's leading physicists.
questions.explanation:
(b) despite decades of
‘Despite’ does not take ‘of’. Therefore, ‘of’ will be removed.
Hence, ‘despite decades of’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The train left before I reached the station.
questions.explanation:
(b) had left before I reached
If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be
in the Past perfect tense (Had + V 3) and the 2nd action must be
in the Simple Past tense(V 2). In the given sentence, ‘train leaving’
is the first action, so it will be written in past perfect tense.
Hence, ‘had left(V 3) before I reached(V 2)’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She met my cousin, whose she later married.
questions.explanation:
(a) whom she later married
‘Whom’ is a relative pronoun used for the object in a relative
clause. In the underlined part, ‘whom’ has been used for the
person she married. Hence, ‘whom she later married’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I decided to call out to various bookstores in the area to see if any of them had the book I needed.
questions.explanation:
(c) call around
The phrasal verb ‘call around’ means to phone different people
or places. The given sentence states that I decided to make
phone calls to various bookstores in the area to see if any of
them had the book I needed. Hence, ‘call around’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: This lesser known heritage building is so beautiful as the Red Fort.
options: This less known heritage building is much beautiful than the Red Fort.
This heritage building is as beautiful as the Red Fort.
This lesser known heritage building is very much beautiful as the Red Fort.
This lesser known heritage building is as much beautiful as the Red Fort.
questions.explanation:
(d) This lesser known heritage building is as much
beautiful as the Red Fort.
‘So…as’ is used with ‘not’ to show that two things are not equal.
‘As…as’ or ‘As much… as’ is used to show that two things are
equal in certain respects. According to option (d), the lesser
known building and the Red fort are equally beautiful. Hence,
option (d) has the correct sentence. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of the parts may contain an error. Select the option that rectifies the error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. It was the home minister of the country who took the decision to change a laws pertaining to migration of people from one state to another.
questions.explanation:
(d) the laws pertaining
Article ‘a’ must be replaced with ‘the’. The ‘laws’ mentioned in
the given sentence are specific and we generally use the definite
article ‘the’ before any specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘the
laws pertaining’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The film received critical acclaim for being a more innovative movie of the year.
questions.explanation:
(d) An innovative
‘More’ must be removed as there is no comparison in this
sentence. Article ‘a’ must be replaced with article ‘an’ as we use
‘an’ before words starting with a vowel sound (an apple, an
umbrella, an MBA). Hence, ‘an innovative’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I will definitely return your notes at Saturday evening.
questions.explanation:
(d) return your notes by
Preposition ‘by’ is used to indicate a deadline or a specific time
before which the action will be completed. The given sentence
states that the notes will be returned by evening. Hence, ‘return
your notes by’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: My sister resembles to my mother a lot in looks and in temperament.
questions.explanation:
(b) resembles
The verb ‘resembles’ does not take the preposition ‘to’ after it.
Hence, ‘resembles’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Effective communication is a skill that can significant enhance your personal and professional life.
questions.explanation:
(d) which can significantly enhance
The given sentence needs an adverb(significantly) to modify the
verb (enhance) and not an adjective (significant). Hence, ‘which
can significantly enhance’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: We have received no information so far to the main island.
questions.explanation:
(c) so far from
‘From’ is used with ‘receive’ to indicate the source destination or
sender. In the given sentence, ‘the main island’ is the source
destination from which no information has been received so far.
Hence, ‘so far from’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: When he was falsely accused of embezzlement, he was beside himself in anger.
questions.explanation:
(a) No improvement
‘Be beside oneself’ is a phrase which means to be in an
extremely emotional state. The given sentence states that the
person was in an extreme state of anger. Hence, option (a) is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She is married with a rich businessman and has enough money to splurge on luxuries.
questions.explanation:
(b) is married to
‘To’ is used after the verb ‘married’ in the passive voice. Hence,
'is married to' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Sherpas have prospered and come along the way from being just porters to becoming mountaineers.
questions.explanation:
(d) come a long way
The phrase ‘come a long way’ means to make significant
progress or improvement. The given sentence states that
Sherpas have prospered and made significant progress from
being just porters to becoming mountaineers. Hence, ‘come a
long way’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: You have a lot of coconut trees in your village, do you ?
questions.explanation:
(b) don’t you?
According to the “Question Tag rule”, if the statement is positive,
the question tag will be negative & Vice-versa. However, the
sentence and the question tag must be in the same tense.
Similarly, the given sentence is positive so the question tag will
be negative(don’t). Hence, ‘don’t you?’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: By next summer, I will have completed my internship and will have returned to school.
questions.explanation:
(d) returned to school
If two or more verbs are of the same tense then the helping verb
is written only once before the first verb. In the given sentence,
‘will have’ is a helping verb of future perfect tense and has been
used for both verbs (‘completed’ and ‘returned’). Hence, ‘returned
to school’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Tomorrow, they will be take a flight to their dream vacation destination.
questions.explanation:
(d) will be taking a flight
‘Will be / shall be + V ’ is the correct grammatical structure of
ing
Future continuous tense. Hence, ‘will be taking (V ) a flight’ is
ing
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: As bombs keep falling on Gaza, hundreds of thousands of children have been order to flee their homes.
questions.explanation:
(a) have been ordered to flee
‘Subject + has/have + been + V 3’ is the correct grammatical
structure for passive voice of Present perfect tense. ‘Ordered’ is
the correct third form of ‘order’. Hence, ‘have been ordered(V 3) to
flee’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The pollution level ought to keep under control.
questions.explanation:
(c) ought to be kept under
Passive voice is used when the action is performed upon the
subject, not by the subject. ‘Ought to + be + V ’ is the correct
3
passive form. Hence, ‘ought to be kept(V ) under’ is the most
3
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: This is the challenge task I have ever encountered.
questions.explanation:
(b) most challenging
Definite article ‘the’ is used for a specific or particular thing and
before a superlative degree adjective. ‘Most challenging’ is the
correct superlative degree of ‘challenging’. Hence, ‘most
challenging’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Ashoka was not only a great warrior but also a very wiser ruler.
questions.explanation:
(d) wise
‘Very’ is a positive adverb and takes a positive degree adjective
after it. Hence, ‘wise’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Cinema provides the most universal entertainment.
questions.explanation:
(b) a universal
There are some adjectives that can not be written in
comparative or superlative degree. These adjectives are called
absolute or non-gradable adjectives. Some examples are
universal, absolute, complete, perfect, empty, full, etc. Hence, ‘a
universal’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He is taller and most handsome than his friend.
questions.explanation:
(b) more
If two or more adjectives are joined with a conjunction, these
adjectives are written in the same degree. In the given sentence,
‘and’ joins two adjectives, out of which one is comparative
degree(taller). Therefore, the second adjective will also be
written in comparative degree. ‘More handsome’ is the correct
comparative degree of ‘handsome’. Hence, ‘more’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Lots of kids (was visualised) crossing the road when the bus arrived.
questions.explanation:
(d) were seen
According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular
subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always
takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘lots of kids’ is a plural
subject that will take ‘were’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘were seen’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The use of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides began after the Green Revolution.
options: A practice of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides
The custom of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides
Consumption of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides
The usage of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides
questions.explanation:
(d) The usage of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides
‘Use’ means the act of utilizing something for a specific purpose
while ‘Usage’ means the customary or habitual manner in which
something is utilized. Hence, ‘The usage of chemicals,
insecticides and pesticides’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

(b) There are three cars parked outside: an Mercedes, a Jaguar

questions.prompt: He is faster than smarter.
questions.explanation:
(a) more fast than smart
When there is a comparison between two qualities of a single
person or thing, we do not use normal comparative degree. E.g.-
more smart than beautiful(not ‘smarter than beautiful’). Similarly,
the given sentence compares two qualities, ‘fast’ and ‘smart’.
Hence, ‘more fast and smart’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The Taj Mahal is one of the much popular seven wonders of the world.
questions.explanation:
(c) most
“One of the + Superlative degree adjective + Plural Subject” is
grammatically the correct structure. For example, one of the
best men, one of the greatest kings, one of the worst phones,
etc. Hence, ‘most’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She trusted her husband but he stabbed her in the neck when he usurped her inheritance.
questions.explanation:
(b) stabbed her in the back
‘Stabbed her in the back’ is the correct idiom that means to be
unfaithful or disloyal to. The given sentence states that she
trusted her husband but he was unfaithful to her when he
usurped her inheritance. Hence, ‘stabbed her in the back’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I like to read books, but my brother prefers to watching movies.
questions.explanation:
(b) to watch
We generally use an infinitive(V 1) with the preposition ‘to’. Hence,
‘to watch’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: This case is serious. You need to look into this matter; otherwise, the situation will get out of control soon.
questions.explanation:
(b) No substitution.
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The village Seoni is located 113 km away from the capital city of MP, Bhopal.
options: adjacent from city capital of MP, Bhopal
proximate from capital of MP, Bhopal
near from the city capital of MP, Bhopal
far from the capital city of MP, Bhopal
questions.explanation:
(d) far from the capital city of MP, Bhopal
‘Far’ means situated at a distance or away from a place. Hence,
‘far from the capital city of MP, Bhopal’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Kiran's teacher was doubtful on her success.
questions.explanation:
(b) doubtful of
‘Of’ is a fixed preposition used after the word ‘doubtful’. Hence,
‘doubtful of’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Harry is the one sitting on the corner.
questions.explanation:
(a) in
‘In’ is used to indicate the location or position of an object or a
person. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘corner’ is the position of
Harry. Hence, ‘in’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The Board of Film Analysts vituperated the novice Indonesian film-maker and cancelled its nomination for the 'Golden Globe Award'.
options: dealt in a delicate and polite manner
recognised and praised the talent of
censured with harsh and abusive language
questions.explanation:
(c) Vituperated - censured with harsh and abusive
language. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Naina is leaving and I am think to apply for her job.
questions.explanation:
(c) thinking about applying
‘Am’ is a helping verb of Present Continuous Tense and
‘is/am/are + V ing ’ is the correct grammatical structure. ‘About’ is
used to introduce the topic or subject of discussion or
consideration. Also, we always use a gerund (V ing ) after a
preposition. Hence, ‘thinking(V ing ) about applying(V ing )’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Malati has a difficult job, but she does it good.
questions.explanation:
(d) well
The given sentence needs an adverb(well) to modify the
meaning of the verb ‘does’, not an adjective(good). Hence, ‘well’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He travelled the whole world, but found piece at home.
questions.explanation:
(d) peace
‘Piece’ means a portion of an object or a material while ‘peace’
means a state of being calm and free from any kind of worry or
disturbance.The word ‘peace’ makes the sentence meaningful.
Hence, ‘peace’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Farmers have harvested wheat by using whatever labour that was available to them.
questions.explanation:
(d) by using limited labour
‘Limited’ means a small quantity or number of something. The
given sentence states that farmers have harvested their wheat
by using a small number of labourers. Hence, ‘by using limited
labour’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: You can become confident to speak English within one year.
questions.explanation:
(b) confident in speaking
‘In’ is used after the word ‘confident’ to show the specific area or
subject in which someone is confident. Hence, ‘confident in
speaking’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The unexpected turn beside the project put the company in a big financial crisis.
questions.explanation:
(d) in the project
‘In’ is used to indicate involvement while ‘beside’ is used to show
that two things are close to each other. The given passage talks
about the impact of unexpected change in the project. Hence,
‘in the project’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Politics and money go together in this country.
questions.explanation: (b) Go hand in hand - go together. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The decision to engage in an armed conflict is tacit.
questions.explanation: (d) Tacit - implied without being stated. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The cat climbed a tree and perched itself on a branch.
questions.explanation:
(c) No substitution required
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fifty rupees feels too much for such a pen.
questions.explanation:
(a) seems
‘Feels’ is used for the sense of touch or emotion and ‘seems’ is
used to show what something appears to be. The word ‘seems’
makes the sentence meaningful. Hence, ‘seems’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Despite of an injury, he won the match.
questions.explanation:
(b) Despite
‘Despite’ means in spite of and it doesn't take any preposition
with it. Hence, ‘Despite’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Lily has dedicate her life towards becoming a doctor.
questions.explanation:
(c) has dedicated
“Has/Have/Had + V (third form of the verb)” is the correct
3
grammatical structure. However, the third form of ‘dedicate’ is
‘dedicated’. Hence, ‘has dedicated(V )’ is the most appropriate
3
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Health insurance are important today since anyone can face a medical emergency without warning.
questions.explanation:
(b) is important
According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular
subject always takes a singular verb. Similarly, ‘Health insurance’
is a singular subject that will take ‘is’ as a singular verb. Hence,
‘is important’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: It was a quite afternoon, so Dan decided to take a nap.
questions.explanation:
(a) a quiet
‘Quite’ is used to emphasize the degree or extent of something
and ‘quiet’ describes something that makes no noise. Similarly,
in the given sentence, it is stated that it was a quiet afternoon.
Hence, ‘a quiet’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: People say different things at different times.
options: say diverse things at different times
says whimsical things at different times
should say fanciful things at different times
says delectable things at different times
questions.explanation:
(a) say diverse things at different times
‘Different’ is used to indicate that two or more things are not the
same or not alike in some way. whereas ‘diverse’ means a wide
range of differences within a group or a set of things. Hence,
‘say diverse things at different times’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Andrew will playing basketball at the college tournament.
questions.explanation:
(c) is playing
‘Is/am/are + V ’ is the correct grammatical structure for
ing
Present Continuous Tense. ‘Andrew’ is a singular subject that
will take ‘is’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘is playing(V ing)’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Selling, purchasing, and using an illegally copied product is a criminal offence.

questions.prompt: With all their little comforts destroyed, the survivors were thrown still farther back into barbarism.

questions.explanation:
(b) still further back into barbarism
‘Farther’ is used to indicate the physical distance while ‘further’
is used to indicate the figurative/metaphorical distance. Hence,
‘still further back into barbarism’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He said that I have finished my work.
questions.explanation:

The given sentence is an example of indirect speech as the
conjunction 'that' has been used after the verb 'said'. As per the
rules of Indirect speech, the pronouns 'I' and ‘My’ change into
'He' and ‘His’ and ‘Present perfect (have + V ) changes to past
3
perfect (had + V ). Hence, 'he had finished his homework' is the
3
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Many great people born in that small village.
questions.explanation:
(d) were born
We generally use the passive voice when the subject is unknown
or unimportant. According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”,
a plural subject always takes a plural verb. Similarly, ‘people’ is a
plural subject that will take ‘were’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘were
born’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: It is true that learning English is essential for professionals to survived the national and international competitions.
questions.explanation:
(d) for surviving
‘For’ is used to indicate the purpose or reason of something.
Similarly, the given sentence states the purpose of learning
English. We generally use gerund(V ) after a preposition(for).
ing
Hence, ‘for surviving(V )’ is the most appropriate answer.
ing (Correct)

questions.prompt: Peer pressure is bound to effect most of us both positively and negatively.
questions.explanation:
(b) to affect most of us
We generally use the first form of the verb(V ) after the
1
preposition ‘to’. ‘Affect’ is the verb form of the noun ‘effect’.
Hence, ‘to affect(V ) most of us’ is the most appropriate answer.
1 (Correct)

questions.prompt: The pandemic has challenged education systems to ensure learning continuity, substantially increasing the demands placed on teachers.

questions.prompt: Mohan unknowingly altered salt instead of sugar to the dessert making it taste terrible.
questions.explanation:
(a) added salt instead of sugar
‘Alter’ means to change the form of something & ‘add’ means to
put in an additional element or ingredient. The word ‘added’ is a
more precise and clear choice in this sentence. Hence, ‘added
salt instead of sugar’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: No sooner did he finished his examination than he left for his cricket training centre.
options: no sooner than he did finished
questions.explanation:
(a) no sooner did he finish
“Do/does/did + V 1 “ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence,
‘no sooner did he finish’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The Delhi administration is seriously worried about the warning to civic health posed by the polluted waters of Yamuna.
questions.explanation:
(d) the threat to civic health
The phrase ‘the threat to civic health’ means the potential danger
or risk to the well-being and overall health of a city. Hence, ‘the
threat to civic health’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The food was too salty eat this morning.
questions.explanation:

‘Too + adjective + to + V 1 ’ is the correct grammatical structure.
Hence, ‘to eat(V 1 )’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: You are always try with jump over the wall.
questions.explanation:
(c) trying to jump
The given sentence is an example of Present Continuous
Tense(Plural Sub. + are + V ing). We generally use the preposition
‘to’ with the verb ‘try’ for an activity. Hence, ‘trying(V ing) to jump’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: They are sell their company's products to people.
questions.explanation:
(b) are selling their company's
We use ‘V-ing’ with the helping verb ‘is/am/are’ in the Present
Continuous Tense. Hence, “are selling(V-ing) their company’s” is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Virtual reality is the creation of a virtual environment presented to our senses in such a way that we experience it as if we were really there.

questions.prompt: Larger emissions of greenhouse gases lead to higher concentrations in the atmosphere.
questions.explanation:
(d) No substitution required.
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: No sooner had the sun risen over the horizon when the birds began to chirp and the squirrels started to scamper around the park.
questions.explanation:
(d) than the birds began
‘No sooner….than’ is a fixed conjunction pair. Hence, ‘than the
birds began’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I considered Geography as an easier subject.
questions.explanation:
(d) an easy
‘An easier’ must be replaced with ‘an easy.’ We need to use a
positive degree of adjective as there is no comparison of
‘geography’ with another subject in the given sentence. Hence,
‘an easy’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Rashmi works at the hospital, don't she?
questions.explanation:
(c) doesn't she?
According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular
subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always
takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘she’ is a singular
pronoun that will take ‘does’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘doesn’t
she’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the word segment which substitutes the bracketed word correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. I (am here) since 1981.

We generally use Perfect Tense or Perfect Continuous Tense
when the time period(for) or the starting point(since) of an
action is given in a sentence. 'Be' is a stative verb and stative
verbs can not be used in continuous tense. Therefore, Present
Perfect Tense(has/have + V ) will be used. Hence, 'have been(V )
3 3
here' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Teenage is that phase of life when you are proposed to the world outside.
questions.explanation:
(a) you are exposed to
‘Proposed’ means to suggest or put forward an idea while
‘exposed’ means to be introduced to something new or
unfamiliar. The given sentence states during teenage years,
individuals are introduced to the world. Hence, ‘exposed’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Very early in the morning, at the beginning of January, Opu was lying in bed waiting for the sun having rose.
options: waited for the sun having rose
waiting for the sun to rise
questions.explanation:
(d) waiting for the sun to rise
We generally use the infinitive form of the verb “to + V 1 ” to
combine two actions. Similarly, in the given sentence, the two
actions are ‘waiting’ and ‘rising’. Hence, ‘waiting for the sun to
rise’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Newton, after seeing the apple falling from a tree, began to wonder whether if it moved towards the earth and not upwards towards the sky.
questions.explanation:
(d) began to wonder why
The phrase 'began to wonder why' means started thinking about
the reason behind the happening of some event. The given
sentence states that Newton started thinking about the reason
for the fall of the apple towards the Earth, not towards the sky.
Hence, 'began to wonder why' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the funny films of all time.
questions.explanation:
(b) funniest
“One of the + Superlative degree adjective (best, worst, etc) +
Plural Noun” is grammatically the correct structure. For example,
one of the best men, one of the greatest kings, one of the worst
phones, etc. Hence, ‘funniest’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If I hand her a flower and say, "Give it to mamma," she take it to her mother.
questions.explanation:
(b) takes it
According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular
subject always takes a singular verb. Similarly, ‘she’ is a singular
pronoun that will take ‘takes’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘takes it’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The new chairman of the company announced attracted bonus for the employees on the occasion of the new year.
options: announced an attractive bonus for the employees
announcing attracted bonus for the employees
announced attracting bonus for the employees
questions.explanation:
(b) announced an attractive bonus for the employees
‘Attracted’ must be replaced with the adjective ‘attractive’ as we
need to use an adjective to qualify the noun ‘bonus.’ Hence,
‘announced an attractive bonus for the employees’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Rishi asked Karan will he get a new football for him ?
options: would he get a new football for him?
if he would get a new football for him.
if would he get a new football for him?
if he will get a new football for him?
questions.explanation:
(b) if he would get a new football for him.
In indirect speech, we generally use ‘if’ while changing the
interrogative sentence and ‘will’ is changed into ‘would’. Also, the
interrogative sentence is changed into an assertive sentence.
Hence, ‘if he would get a new football for him’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If you need any help tomorrow, let him knows.
questions.explanation:
(a) let me know
‘Let + objective case pronoun(me/him/us) + V 1’ is the correct
grammatical structure. Hence, ‘let me know(V 1)’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Helena loves to dig and played in the dirt like any other child.
questions.explanation:
(d) play in the dirt
According to the ‘Rule of Parallelism’, two or more verbs must be
in the same form if they are connected with one another.
Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘and’ connects two verbs 'dig(V 1)’
and ‘played’. Therefore, ‘play(V 1)’ must be used in place of
‘played’. Hence, ‘play in the dirt’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The development of skills can contribute to structural transformation and economic growth in enhance employability and labour productivity and helping countries to become more competitive.
questions.explanation:
(c) by enhancing employability
‘By’ is a preposition that indicates the means or method by
which something is done. A preposition is always followed by a
gerund(V 1-ing). Hence, ‘by enhancing employability’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I used a variety of sources to find the more cheap flight.
questions.explanation:
(c) cheapest
We generally use article ‘the’ with a superlative degree and the
correct superlative degree of ‘cheap’ is ‘cheapest’. Hence,
‘cheapest’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: His claim to be the smartly kid in the school was a bit hyperbole !
questions.explanation:
